description: Editor assistance for WTF configuration. Runtime validation remains authoritative; schema default annotations do not apply inherited settings.

change.description: Replace the message on a registered workspace by name or ID in the current repository. Omit NAME to change the current workspace, including from a subdirectory. --message replaces the description; an empty string clears it. Without a requested change, show help without modifying anything or running hooks. Does not create or prepare workspaces. Examples: wtf change testing-msg -m "Picking this up tomorrow"; wtf change testing-msg -m ""; wtf change -m "Picking this up tomorrow".

completion.description: Print a shell script for bash, zsh or fish. Source it in your shell to complete commands, aliases, flags, live workspace names and configured project tasks. Workspace and task matches include fuzzy subsequences. No hooks or network lookups run. Example: source <(wtf completion bash). See docs/completion.md for installation and shell aliases.

doctor.description: Report configuration, tool readiness and workspace health independently, including before workspace registration. Parse strict TOML and compile the selected Lua entrypoint without executing it. Check JJ identity, GitHub authentication and the repository's Codex Linear MCP connection. Inspect retained workspace stages, claims and identity. Checks are bounded; authentication may contact GitHub and Linear. Does not run hooks, register workspaces, snapshot JJ state or repair anything. Invalid configuration, required JJ prerequisites or unhealthy workspace state fail; unregistered workspaces and optional GitHub/Linear warnings do not. Example: wtf doctor --json.

list.description:
Browse active workspaces with arrow keys; Enter selects, Esc cancels. The view paginates to your terminal size. list and ls are the same command. An optional NAME resolves a workspace directly.

Inside a repository, show its workspaces; from a parent directory, show repositories beneath it. --global includes all registered repositories, --all includes unavailable and removed records.

--hook adds local stages, not CI. --pr adds GitHub PR status; each invocation performs a bounded live lookup. JSON and redirected output never prompt. With shell integration, selection changes your directory.

Examples:
  wtf list
  wtf ls -p
  wtf ls --all --json

new.description: Bare names resolve beside the registered main repository, even from another workspace or subdirectory, without a repository prefix or suffix. Explicit relative paths resolve from the current directory; absolute paths also work. An existing JJ workspace root is registered and prepared; a missing path creates an owned JJ workspace at that exact location, named after its basename. --from defaults to trunk() and only applies to creation. Existing directories that are not workspace roots are rejected. Both modes run the init override; only creation runs the new override, which may block before mutation. Repeated calls preserve identity, ownership and reusable stages. JSON registration codes are initialized or already_initialized. Project arguments after -- keep their case. Examples: wtf new .; wtf new agent-a -f @ -- --compose. New workspaces copy .wtf/config.toml, schema.json, hooks/ and tasks/ from the invoking workspace before initialization and creation callbacks, with independent files and local ignore rules. Declarative phase hooks also inherit from ancestor .wtf/config.toml files, outermost first; their imports remain in the declaring hook package. Local artifacts and runtime state are excluded. Existing-workspace preparation preserves its configuration.

remove.description:
Open an inline multi-select cleanup picker. Space toggles a workspace; f toggles force mode to discard remaining source changes; a selects clean workspaces verified in main/master; Enter reviews, then confirms removal. Current and adopted workspaces are protected. Changes outside main/master block removal unless force mode is enabled in the picker. Integration uses local JJ ancestry or a fresh merged GitHub PR with an exact matching head and main/master base. Local bookmarks and remote bookmarks reflect their last fetched state. Normal JJ snapshotting captures on-disk changes during inspection.

An explicit NAME removes one workspace directly. JSON and redirected output with no NAME report cleanup candidates without removing them. Teardown hooks and identity/resource checks are revalidated for each removal. Failures retain cleanup state.

Examples:
  wtf remove
  wtf rm agent-a --json
  wtf remove --json

Inside a repository, removal uses that repository. From a parent directory, it includes registered repositories beneath it, just like switch; no --global flag is required. Repeated names require a workspace ID or running inside the intended repository.

setup.description: Create .wtf in the current directory with config.toml, the generated editor schema, a self-contained AGENTS.md reference, its template checksum, and completely empty hooks and tasks directories. Its .gitignore contains only * so all scaffold files stay local and untracked. Config/schema edits are preserved; repeated setup fills in missing files and refreshes guides matching the previously installed checksum. Customized or unknown guides are preserved with an update-available report. The guide and checksum are inherited by newly created workspaces. Uses the installed binary's embedded template without a network lookup. Does not run hooks, install dependencies or register a workspace. No repository is required. Use setup teardown to remove the local .wtf directory after a yes/no confirmation. Examples: wtf setup; wtf setup --json; wtf setup teardown.

setup teardown.description: Remove the entire .wtf directory and its contents from the current directory after an interactive yes/no confirmation, defaulting to No. Works even with broken configuration. Does not run hooks or change workspace registration, source outside .wtf, or shared state. Symlink targets are never removed. JSON and redirected output report confirmation_required without deleting anything; a missing .wtf is a successful no-op. Example: wtf setup teardown.

commands.description: Defaults for registered command flags. Precedence is global, outer parent, nearest parent, leaf, then explicit CLI flags. These schema defaults are annotations and do not perform the merge.

invocation.description: Hooks around execution commands. Inspection, help, version and setup teardown never invoke callbacks. Wraps command-specific phases.

after.description: Ordered modules run after a successful operation. A failure stops the sequence and fails the command.

before.description: Ordered modules run before the operation. A failure blocks the operation. Modules return function(event).

failed.description: Modules run on failure with event.error. All are attempted; they cannot hide the primary error.

finally.description: Modules run on success or failure. All are attempted with bounded cleanup time, including after cancellation.

hooks.description: Compatibility shorthand for after. For new, runs inside native creation; other surfaces run these before explicit after hooks. Modules return function(event), names preserve case, and ancestor phase lists run before workspace lists. Prefer explicit phase arrays.
